content: Masjid Istiqlal is South-East Asia's largest mosque — Jakarta's national mosque, capacity 200,000+. Belief tradition: Sunni Islam. Observance type: doctrinal. Notably located directly across from the Catholic Jakarta Cathedral — a symbol of Indonesian religious pluralism. Non-Muslim visitors are welcome outside of prayer times; dress modestly (shoulders + knees covered, headscarf provided for women at the entrance). Free entry; a guide-tip is customary. Do not photograph worshippers mid-prayer.

Borobudur is the world's largest Buddhist temple (9th-century Sailendra dynasty) — a functioning Buddhist site as well as a UNESCO monument. Belief tradition: Theravada + Mahayana Buddhist. Observance type: doctrinal + tourist-facing. Timed entry to upper terraces (foreigner ~US$25–35) since 2022; sunrise access ticketed separately. Local Buddhist community observes Waisak here in May — access restricted that day. Visitors dress modestly, walk clockwise around the stupas, do not touch reliefs.

Prambanan is a 9th-century Hindu temple complex — the largest in Indonesia — dedicated to the Trimurti (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva). Belief tradition: Historical + revived Hindu practice (mostly Balinese Hindus visit for observances). Observance type: doctrinal (revived) + tourist-facing. UNESCO listed. Sarong + sash required for the main temples (rental included with ticket). Combine-ticket with Borobudur available. Dry-season Ramayana ballet in the outdoor amphitheatre most weekends — book ahead.
